subject.title: [Feature]: Skill lifecycle management — auto-optimization on failure + usage-based retirement

question: Should failure-driven skill optimization and usage-based skill retirement be core Skill Workshop behavior, a plugin or ClawHub extension point, or split into narrower follow-up issues?
rationale: Current main partially covers user-correction capture, but the remaining behavior changes product policy, config, persistent state, and possibly privacy-sensitive telemetry.

options.title: Split design first
options.body: Keep this issue open for maintainer design and split failure repair, metrics storage, retirement policy, and ClawHub telemetry into separately owned implementation issues.

options.title: Build in core
options.body: Treat this as core Skill Workshop lifecycle behavior and require a storage, doctor, config, docs, and conservative approval plan before implementation.

options.title: Externalize via APIs
options.body: Keep core lean by adding only the missing plugin or ClawHub hooks needed for external lifecycle managers to own optimization and retirement.

recommendation.title: Split design first
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open for maintainer design and split failure repair, metrics storage, retirement policy, and ClawHub telemetry into separately owned implementation issues.

likelyOwner.reason: Most recent code ownership signal is on the current autocapture and workshop internals that would need to be extended or deliberately kept narrow.
